rv.q: And it passed the ‘good date’ test with flying colours: this show made me feel very happy on the night, and on the morning after.
Tutty (Dear Evan Hansen) and Gift excel, and earn their standing ovation.
Two Strangers is as good a night out in the West End as you can get.
A warm and delightful production that proves that it’s possible to have one’s cake and eat it after all.

Piccadilly Circus was a-buzz last evening as the crowds gathered for the much anticipated opening of TWO STRANGERS (CARRY A CAKE ACROSS NEW YORK) at the Criterion Theatre. This reviewer was unable to see the earlier staging at the Kiln in Kilburn, North London back in November last year.
It’s that rare show in which you really take the characters to heart, and this contrasting pair are beautifully balanced on their parallel journeys to self-acceptance.

An incredible new British musical, Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) is uniquely special, it will melt your heart, and give you hope that your fortune can be changed by someone you’ve yet to meet.
The score is fresh and tuneful, the lyrics witty and wise, and the sensational stars breathe real life into it all.

cn.t: Critics embrace this charming British musical as an intimate, heartfelt romcom treat. The two-hander wins praise for its gentle charm, offbeat sweetness, and the chemistry between its leads in Tim Jackson's appealing production.
